Proves that a preset is resolved in the REQUEST'S zone, on both axes at once. The pinned `now` is `2026-08-12T23:30:00Z`; in `Europe/Paris` (UTC+02:00 in August) that instant is 2026-08-13T01:30 local, so "today" is **2026-08-13**, not the 2026-08-12 a UTC-based implementation would pick. The window is the local day `[2026-08-13, 2026-08-14)`, whose absolute instants are `2026-08-12T22:00:00Z` and `2026-08-13T22:00:00Z`.

Two distinct bugs are pinned out by this one case: computing the calendar day in UTC (or in the server process's own `TZ`, which SEM-4 explicitly forbids) gives the wrong DAY; computing the right day but emitting midnight-UTC instants gives the right day shifted by two hours. Both return a visibly different row set from what the user's grid shows. `zone: "Europe/Paris"` on each `datetimeValue` records which zone produced the instants — provenance only; the compiled artifacts contain no `AT TIME ZONE`/`$dateTrunc.timezone`/ES `time_zone` clause anywhere.
